nonBlocking: Swift release build is unverified in this review; the verdict covers source correctness only. The GemmaForge.forge byte-count guard (`try? ... .fileSize ?? -1` compared against an Int) relies on optional promotion and reads as fragile; confirm it compiles and behaves as intended under the current toolchain.

CLI --rehash-model pre-dispatch guard requires exactly one of --file/--gguf. Any command in modelDigestCommands that legitimately accepts both flags (or neither, e.g. q4-lower with an unbound op) will be refused; confirm each listed command's flag set, and confirm per-command parsers do not reject --rehash-model as an unknown flag after the pre-dispatch handling.
model-digest with both --cache-only and --rehash-model hashes first and then reads the record; harmless but the combination could be rejected as contradictory for clarity.
Cache record disclosure is printed to stdout by cachedModelDigest; verify no model command emits machine-parsed JSON on the same stream (attnqual already emits JSON per line, which is fine).

Neither the Swift decoder nor the Python _well_formed check rejects extra keys, although both headers say the record has 'exactly these fields'. Interoperability is unaffected; tighten or reword if strictness is intended.

Canonical path interop depends on realpath(3) bytes on both sides; Unicode normalization of user-supplied paths (NFC vs NFD) is handled identically only because both call realpath on the same input. A test with a non-ASCII model path would make this explicit.
GemmaCompositeForge.isConsistentNoWin is declared throws but cannot throw; drop the annotation and the try sites.

Q4LaunchSelect.persist falls back to Q4LaunchSchedule(width: 1) when no finalist passed; that artifact cannot validate (no accepted component entry). The non-diagnostic path throws earlier, but the diagnostic path can persist an unvalidatable artifact; pre-existing behavior, worth a guard.
rationale: The change implements the required semantics consistently across Swift and Python: the model SHA-256 is computed once from actual bytes on the first cache miss, persisted under a SHA-256(realpath) key with a per-key flock, reused on every later lookup without reading model bytes and without stat/size/mtime invalidation, refreshed only by an explicit --rehash-model (CLI, attnqual) or LEVIATHAN_REHASH_MODEL=1 (Python), and malformed, mismatched, or retired-policy records fail with a refresh instruction rather than a silent rehash. Record format, key derivation, timestamp format, lock file, bounded reads, and atomic replace match between ModelDigestCache.swift and model_digest_cache.py, and the cross-process Python test plus the Swift gate on symlink/mutation/deletion/retired-policy cover the interop surface. The retired none-unverified value is not representable in either language, schema versions are bumped to 3 everywhere, and the policy is encoded into body/plan digests and required on decode. Numerical gates, the fixed 2% policy, pristine-runner gating, atomic install with prior-state restore, and prepared-execution binding are unchanged. The CLI refresh runs exactly once before the workflow and all nested lookups reuse the refreshed record. Remaining items are flag-handling edge cases that cannot be verified without the full main.swift and small cleanups, none of which affect the stated semantics.
